elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly permits IBM to terminate the Agreement, in whole or in part, for convenience.

elements.element: Customer may exercise its termination-for-convenience right on thirty (30) days' prior written notice.
elements.evidence: IBM may terminate upon “thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL.”

elements.element: Customer must receive a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees attributable to the period after termination.
elements.evidence: MSL must refund amounts prepaid by IBM for the period after the effective date of termination, which operatively provides the required time-based pro-rata refund.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: No operative language grants MSL a convenience-termination right during the initial or renewal terms. Its existing right is limited to preventing renewal through end-of-term notice; the separate mid-term termination provision is for cause.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly grants IBM a termination-for-convenience right.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience notice period must be between sixty (60) and ninety (90) days.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause requires only thirty (30) days' notice, not the fallback range of 60–90 days.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee imposed on Customer must not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause imposes no early-termination fee, so no fee exceeds the permitted cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: MSL has no mid-term convenience right; its no-cause exit operates through notice preventing automatic renewal at the end of a term.

elements.element: Vendor's end-of-term termination-for-convenience right must require ninety (90) days' notice.
elements.evidence: The renewal provision requires six (6) months' written notice rather than 90 days.

result.reason: The operative language fully satisfies the preferred position: IBM receives a 30-day convenience exit and a refund of prepaid amounts allocable to the post-termination period, while MSL receives no mid-term convenience right. It does not literally satisfy the fallback notice periods. The redline preserves unrelated terms and creates no contradiction, but it is not strictly minimal because “in whole or in part” adds a partial-termination right beyond what was required. The low drafting-quality score reflects the unnecessary expansion and the potential operational ambiguity of partial termination without specifying how affected prepaid amounts or services are allocated.
